svg.title: Fabric Spark autoscale internals
svg.desc: Fabric Spark autoscale and dynamic allocation internals: Initial reserve at submission, task backlog evaluation, bounded scale-up, idle detection, safe executor decommission, shuffle block retention risks, and lifecycle billing timeline.
svg.text: Fabric Spark Autoscale & Dynamic Allocation Internals
Scaling decision loop · Min/Max node bounds · Executor decommission · Shuffle retention pin · Billing timeline
ZONE 1: DYNAMIC ALLOCATION DECISION CYCLE (UNDER LOAD)

g.title: Spark job demand — A notebook or Spark Job Definition submits work against a configured pool.
Minimum executor reserve — Dynamic allocation reserves executors from the pool minimum at submission.
Tasks exceed capacity? — Dynamic allocation grows executors when runnable tasks outstrip capacity.
g.text: • Compare runnable tasks to active slots

g.title: Scale toward maximum — The pool adds workers only within its configured maximum.
g.text: • Adds worker nodes up to configured max
• Size is fixed; changes count only

g.title: Idle executors detected? — Executors become release candidates after work completes or idles.
g.text: • Evaluates unused worker nodes after stage finishes

g.title: Decommission safely — Fabric enables executor decommission by default for automatic scale-down.
g.text: • Idle nodes shut down without dropping active session

g.title: Shuffle blocks pin workers — Local shuffle data can prevent release until downstream readers finish.

g.text: Fabric only meters active execution wall-clock time. Idle pre-warm, Azure node acquisition, context start, and post-job deallocation are 100% free.

svg.text: Fabric Atlas — Original Diagram, August 2026. Sourced from Microsoft Learn: Apache Spark in Microsoft Fabric & Autoscale Internals.
